identification: Victorian figured rosewood ladies' travelling dressing box, c.1850-1880, 30 x 23 x 16 cm, brass-lined edges, vacant brass lid plaque, brass escutcheons, key present (on string), lower drawer with velvet-lined compartments and a velvet pad. Gilt-tooled red velvet lid lining (creased, no mirror seen). Lift-out tray with brass side handles. Fittings counted: 7 cut glass bottles/jars (4 with cut-glass star stoppers, 3 with plain flat white-metal screw/push lids: one in the back row, two round ones in the tray), 2 rectangular white-metal boxes with bright-cut foliate engraving and vacant oval cartouches (one long, about toothbrush/comb size; one smaller, card-case/soap size), 2 mother-of-pearl handled tools (buttonhook and a pick/tweezer), 2 velvet-topped ring/pin compartments. Looks complete.

viewing_check: Turn over the two engraved boxes and look inside their lids, and check the three jar lids, for hallmarks (lion passant, town mark, date letter, maker); EPNS/EP or a maker's name with no lion means plate, and copper showing through worn high spots also means plate. Count glass for chips or cracked stoppers. Check the lock works with the key, the tray lifts, the drawer runs, the rosewood veneer for lifting or cracks, and whether the lid has a mirror behind the velvet.
